sweep_summary: Single sweep item, Robbins 1991 'Lexicalized Metrical Foot Structure in Maidu' (PASC 2:95-116), is squarely about Northeast Maidu word stress and is the primary origin (with Hayes 1995:261) of the CVC-heavy initial/second-syllable rule the catalog carries via StressTyp2; it remains unobtainable online: UCSC's Linguistics Research Center page confirms PASC vol. 2 (Mester & Robbins eds., 1991, vii+116 pp., paper, no ISBN) is print-only with no eScholarship copy (only vols 6-7 are digitized), Google Books holds the 1991 volume with no page view (id EsZwAAAAIAAJ), and Crossref/Semantic Scholar/archive.org have no record; Hayes 1995 (Google Books id ST1JpDcrR3sC) could not be searched inside (captcha). Dixon's 1911 Maidu sketch in Boas's Handbook (already on file), Phonetics sections 2-4 pp. 684-687, says nothing about stress placement. No new first-hand stress statement was read; the catalog's deciding source (Shipley 1964, page-image) stands. Acquisition priority for Robbins 1991: high (ILL from a library holding PASC 2, or request from UCSC LRC / sasc@ucsc.edu).

audit.reasoning: Quote check passes: every fragment of the deciding quotation is verbatim in the held Shipley 1964 scanned/page images at the cited pages (6, 10-11, 21, 22; Sect.321 p.16 too). The deciding source is the standard reference grammar and nothing newer or instrumental on Maidu stress surfaced (CrossRef, archive.org; Glottolog's list has no later grammar or phonology). The record is honest about the split: Shipley = phonemic/lexical stress with root-shape tendencies; the CVC-heavy I/S;I rule is a Robbins 1991/Hayes 1995 reanalysis reached only through StressTyp2, and StressTyp2's 'Shipley 1964:13' passage is a paraphrase not found in Shipley. Hence 'weight-hedged' is the right call and not at risk, but the weight half rests on two unheld theoretical sources; obtaining Robbins 1991 (high) or Hayes 1995:261 (medium) and re-reading would let the record quote the rule from its actual author and report
